headline: My KAIST exchange, from “should I apply?” to credits back at DTU
intro: I spent the fall 2025 semester on exchange at KAIST in Daejeon, South Korea, in the third year of my bachelor's line in Artificial Intelligence and Data at DTU. I picked KAIST because I love Korean food and culture, it's fairly prestigious, and I wanted the challenge of a new study culture, new people and new places.

scores.why: The first days are stressful, and after that it's super fun
My two favourite courses were excellent, but the exams test memorisation hard
About 200 exchange students in my cohort, and I never felt lonely
Very cheap, with a gym and study space, but I shared a double room and there's no kitchen
Kaimaru and cheap Korean barbecue, often all-you-can-eat
Paper forms everywhere, and getting the residence card was "one of the biggest messes ever"
No tuition, a dorm that cost me about 4,000 DKK for the whole semester, and cheap food

tips.text: Arrive two days early and rest before orientation.
Have Uber installed when you land, which "makes everything 100 times easier".
Do the forms on day one and give them the whole day.
Take the residence card shortcut to the immigration office on campus.
Put the registration lottery in your calendar as soon as you're accepted.
Get a real Korean SIM with 30 to 50 GB (gigabytes) of data a month and calling.
Bring a backup international card such as Revolut or Lunar.
Get a bike, because the campus is big and attendance counts.
Pack light and buy clothes in Korea.
Be polite to professors and teaching assistants, who are flexible if you ask nicely.
Don't stress about a bad midterm, since grading is on a curve.
Pick "out-of-distribution" courses, ones you couldn't take at home, and take databases at DTU.
Apply for every grant, the small ones included.
Say yes to everything socially in the first weeks.
Book the airport bus home early and leave Daejeon in the morning.
